truths.CP4:
WITH months AS (
  -- one row per month from June to September 2025
  SELECT DISTINCT month
  FROM mrr_monthly
  WHERE month >= DATE '2025-06-01'
    AND month <= DATE '2025-09-01'
),
accounts_in_window AS (
  -- one row per account with MRR at the end of at least one of those months
  SELECT DISTINCT account_id
  FROM mrr_monthly
  WHERE month >= DATE '2025-06-01'
    AND month <= DATE '2025-09-01'
),
filled AS (
  -- one row per account and month, with 0 for a month without MRR
  SELECT a.account_id, m.month, COALESCE(r.mrr_eur, 0) AS mrr
  FROM accounts_in_window AS a
  CROSS JOIN months AS m
  LEFT JOIN mrr_monthly AS r
    ON r.account_id = a.account_id
   AND r.month = m.month
),
compared AS (
  -- one row per account and month, with its MRR at the end of the month before
  SELECT account_id, month, mrr,
         LAG(mrr) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY month) AS mrr_before
  FROM filled
),
new_accounts AS (
  -- one row per account and month in which its first subscription started
  SELECT DISTINCT account_id, CAST(date_trunc('month', event_date) AS DATE) AS month
  FROM subscription_events
  WHERE event_type = 'new'
),
movements AS (
  -- one total per movement over July to September 2025
  SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN c.mrr_before = 0 AND c.mrr > 0 AND n.account_id IS NOT NULL THEN c.mrr ELSE 0 END) AS new_mrr,
         SUM(CASE WHEN c.mrr_before > 0 AND c.mrr > c.mrr_before THEN c.mrr - c.mrr_before ELSE 0 END) AS expansion_mrr,
         SUM(CASE WHEN c.mrr_before > 0 AND c.mrr > 0 AND c.mrr < c.mrr_before THEN c.mrr_before - c.mrr ELSE 0 END) AS contraction_lost,
         SUM(CASE WHEN c.mrr_before > 0 AND c.mrr = 0 THEN c.mrr_before ELSE 0 END) AS churn_lost
  FROM compared AS c
  LEFT JOIN new_accounts AS n
    ON n.account_id = c.account_id
   AND n.month = c.month
  WHERE c.month >= DATE '2025-07-01'
)
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * (churn_lost + contraction_lost) / (new_mrr + expansion_mrr), 1) AS taken_back_pct
FROM movements

CP1.explanation: Only the subscription events show whether this is the account's first subscription; mrr_monthly starts in January 2024, so an account that left that month and came back has no earlier row and would wrongly count as new.

CP5.explanation: The bridge shows how much churn and contraction took back of what sales booked, so the deck names the larger loss and its accounts; it shows neither that more new sales nor the price rise would close the gap.
